name: Japan MSCA payments and distribution (Dec 2025)
plain: Japan's smartphone act lets apps use other stores, payments and links from Dec 2025.
meaning: Opens Japan to alternative app marketplaces, alternative payment processors and links. Apple still vets marketplaces; fees changed.

android.permission: Play Console: alternative billing and external offers for Japan under MSCA
android.prompt_ui: Google shows choice screens as required
android.note: Google announced Japan changes aligned to the Dec 18 2025 date.

ios.prompt_ui: Apple choice screens for browser and search in Japan
ios.store_policy: Apple notarization of marketplace apps; marketplaces must be authorised
ios.api_surface: StoreKit External Purchase, MarketplaceKit, alternative browser engines
ios.note: Released Dec 12 2025 in iOS 26.2; fees reported as 10 or 21 percent plus 5 percent payment processing.

limits.headline: Can offer other app stores, payment options and web links to buyers in Japan
limits.user_action: You see a choice screen, or tap a link to pay outside the main store
can: Offer a different payment company at checkout
Send you to its own web page to pay
Let you install apps from a third party store (iPhone, with Apple's approval)
Show browser or store choice screens that Apple or Google require
cannot: Skip Apple's checks of other stores on iPhone
Avoid all fees, since fees were changed, not removed
limits.reach_label: One purchase or install at a time
limits.differs: On iPhone Apple still approves other stores and charges reduced fees; on Android Google runs alternative billing and external offer programs.

story.what_it_is: A Japanese law that lets iPhone and Android apps use other app stores, payment systems and web links.
story.for_you: Most people in Japan see little at first. Over time some apps may offer another app store, a different way to pay, or a link to buy on the web. You choose, and prices or trust may differ.
story.for_makers: The law forces Apple and Google to open their stores in Japan from December 2025. Developers can cut fees, reach people through other stores, and send buyers to their own checkout. The platforms still charge some fees and run safety checks.

use_cases.example: A Japanese mobile game studio sells gems through its own web shop link and offers a small bonus for paying there, instead of using the in app store.
A manga reading app lets subscribers pay through a Japanese card processor and links to its own site for a cheaper yearly plan.
A shopping app offers the same checkout it uses on the web, so loyalty points work the same inside the app.
A big game publisher ships its game through a third party store that bundles launch day deals and free currency.
A local wallet app is offered as a payment choice next to Apple Pay or Google Pay at checkout.
A small indie developer saves on fees and reinvests the money in new game levels.
Apple and Google scan outside apps for malware and show warnings so people know what they are installing.

story.android_note: Google said it would follow the December 2025 date in Japan with similar changes to Play.
story.ios_note: iOS 26.2 added the Japan changes in December 2025, with Apple still charging reduced fees and running checks.

technical_bounds: Japan only; Apple states notarization remains required
